success_patterns: Archive hit: the clue appeared verbatim in a Jeopardy dump (ROCK "E" | clue | Endless), and the agent copied the bare answer as printed.

No archive hit: the agent found the entity that recurs across the topical passages next to the clue's distinctive details (harpsichord, Jesse Owens, In the Heat of the Night, The King and I) and gave its bare standard name.

A clue that was only a quoted line of verse ("I think that I shall never see a poem lovely as a tree") was answered with its author. Passages printed the line with 'Trees by Joyce Kilmer' attribution.

A leading parenthetical stage direction ('(Jimmy of the Clue Crew at the St. James Theatre...)') was treated as filler. The agent answered from the factual core (musical, Yul Brynner, 1951) and returned the musical, not the theatre or the actor.
A group-defining clue ('these people born between '46 & '64') was answered with the plural label the passages' titles repeat (baby boomers).

A truncated archive snippet plus a tag in another passage ('bluebeard', 'edna st vincent millay') gave the folklore figure. The agent trusted the combination of the clue's anchor (Millay poem) and the recurring entity.

patch.reasoning: The skill already covers archive copying, slot typing and bare-form answers, and the agent applied them well in these successes. Three behaviors are not stated explicitly. First, a clue that is only a quoted line maps to its author. Second, a leading stage-direction parenthetical is filler, not a caption. Third, a defining group clue maps to the plural label the passages use. Stating them in a few short bullets under the existing Rule 1 matches earlier guidance to avoid long bundles. Each edit is one line and conditional on a visible clue feature, so it should not conflict with the existing type-check or trimming rules.

edits.target: - Jokes, asides and filler in the clue ('(If I eat it, can I hear the ocean?)', 'Need help in this subject? Call up...') are decoration.
edits.content: A LEADING parenthetical that describes the video, audio or host ('(Jimmy of the Clue Crew at the St. James Theatre...)') is stage direction: ignore it, and do not answer with the venue or person it names. Only a TRAILING role-and-dates parenthetical is a caption.

edits.target: - If the clue is a fragment, work out what single thing connects it to the context.
edits.content: - A clue that is only a quoted line of verse, lyric or famous quotation (no 'this <noun>' slot) asks for who wrote it. Passages printing the same line under 'Title by Author' give the name; answer the author's bare name, not the poem title or the quote.

edits.target: - A bare date + place (or date + event) fragment such as 'February 6, 1911 in Tampico, Illinois'
edits.content: Likewise, 'these people / these animals' plus a birth-year range, site or audience description asks for the group label the passage titles repeat next to those dates or terms (born 1946-1964 -> 'baby boomers'). Give that plural label, not a famous member or a single year.
